summary.short: Mexico's Federal Economic Competition Law (text consolidated to the reforms of 16-07-2025 and 14-11-2025) prohibits monopolistic practices, illicit concentrations and barriers to competition, requires prior authorization of large mergers, and empowers the Comisión Nacional Antimonopolio to investigate and fine firms. It contains no AI-specific provisions.
summary.long: The Ley Federal de Competencia Económica, a general competition statute published 23 May 2014 and consolidated to the reforms of 16-07-2025 and 14-11-2025, applies to all economic agents and activity nationwide. It defines key terms, including the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones, and creates the Comisión Nacional Antimonopolio, a decentralised body governed by a five-member Pleno with an Autoridad Investigadora. The Comisión may order removal of barriers to competition, regulate access to essential inputs, and determine substantial market power, including designating Agentes Económicos Preponderantes in broadcasting and telecommunications. Book Two prohibits absolute monopolistic practices, which are null by law, and relative practices, and sets rules on relevant markets and illicit concentrations. Book Three governs investigations, trial-type procedures, interim measures, and merger control: concentrations above UMA-denominated thresholds need prior authorisation, with review periods, conditions and exemptions, plus leniency and formal opinions. Title VII sets fines expressed in UMA or as percentages of revenue, disqualification of individuals, and divestiture. The provided text reproduces Articles 1 to 131; later provisions, including Article 134 on damages, appear only in the outline. It contains no AI-specific provisions.

notes: Part 1 of 2: covers the text from the title through Art. 131 (Capítulo IV, Título VII); Part 2 covers the rest. Consolidated text (Texto vigente, last reform DOF 14-11-2025). The registry title says the 2025 decree also reforms the Ley Federal de las Entidades Paraestatales; its amendment text does not appear in this part (only a cross-reference in Art. 125). Many articles are marked 'Se deroga' (e.g., Arts. 5, 14-17, 37-46, 101) and are not coded. Internal inconsistencies: Art. 22 names 'Ley Federal de Responsabilidades de los Servidores Públicos', Arts. 31 and 35 name 'Ley Federal de Responsabilidades Administrativas de los Servidores Públicos', and Art. 51 names 'Ley General de Responsabilidades Administrativas'. The last paragraph of Art. 131 refers to resolutions under Art. 101, which is repealed. Art. 127 XIV cites Art. 94 fracción VII for the desincorporación order; the remedy list in Art. 94 follows fracción VII. Art. 127 mentions the 'Impuesto Sobre la Renta' without naming a statute. Thresholds, obligations, enforcement amounts and events were not coded in this part (not requested). Part 2 covers LFCE Arts. 132-145 (Libro Cuarto, Telecommunications and Broadcasting, added by the 16-07-2025 decree), the appended transitorios of the 2014, 2017, 2021, 16-07-2025 and 14-11-2025 decrees, and expedition formulas. Art. 136 is shown as derogated. The LFPE reform (Artículo Segundo) is not reproduced in this part. Agency and CRT acronyms are used without definition in this part. Many duties depend on the integration of the Comisión Nacional Antimonopolio Pleno, a date not fixed in this text. Art. 143 cross-refers to Art. 127 and transitional Art. 94 and 96 references to the prior LFCE fall outside this part.
